title: Paying for parking by QR code? That code may be a fake sticker
description:
Paying for parking by QR code? Check that it isn't a fake sticker.

Scammers stick their own QR codes on parking meters and pay-and-display machines. The code opens a fake payment page that asks for your card number, expiry date and security code.

This year drivers were warned about fake parking QR codes in Germany (Hannover and the Lower Saxony state police, reported by Stiftung Warentest), Luxembourg City (stickers found on meters in April, reported to the city, CIRCL and police) and New Zealand (Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch). On September 8, 2026, Auckland Transport said: "AT does not use QR codes on any of our parking meters or machines."

Analyst note: a QR code hides the web address, so check where it really goes before you type anything.

Do this tonight:
1. Look for a sticker stuck on top of the machine or sign.
2. Use the official parking app, or pay at the machine itself.
3. If you typed your card into a strange site, call your bank right away, then report it to the police.

Sources
- Auckland Transport media release (Sep 8, 2026): https://at.govt.nz/about-us/news-events/media-centre/2026-media-releases/aucklanders-warned-about-scam-parking-meter-qr-codes
